Discretize a continuous time model

Source: R/discretization.R
ctrl_c2d.Rd

Convert a continuous time model to discrete time with sample interval dt.

Usage

ctrl_c2d(
  sys,
  dt,
  method = c("zoh", "foh", "tustin", "matched"),
  prewarp = NULL
)

Arguments

sys

A continuous time model.

dt

Positive sample interval.

method

One of "zoh", "foh", "tustin" or "matched".

prewarp

Optional prewarping frequency for "tustin".

Value

A discrete time model of the same class as sys ("matched" returns a transfer function).

Details

  • "zoh" (default): exact zero-order hold. The input is held constant between samples and \(A_d = e^{A T}\), \(B_d = \int_0^T e^{A\tau} B\,d\tau\), both read from the matrix exponential of the block matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} T\). This is valid for singular A; the formula \(A^{-1}(A_d - I)B\) is never used.

  • "foh": exact first-order (triangle) hold, for inputs that are linearly interpolated between samples. The discrete state is \(\xi_k = x_k - \Gamma_2 u_k\) (not the physical state), so a physical initial state \(x_0\) corresponds to \(\xi_0 = x_0 - \Gamma_2 u_0\); the matrix \(\Gamma_2\) is stored in the foh_state_map attribute of the result.

  • "tustin": bilinear transformation \(s = \frac{2}{T}\frac{z-1}{z+1}\), optionally prewarped so that the frequency response matches exactly at prewarp rad per time unit.

  • "matched": matched pole-zero mapping \(z = e^{sT}\) for SISO models, with zeros at infinity mapped to \(z = -1\) (all but one, so the result stays strictly proper when the original is) and the gain matched at DC (or at s = j/T when there is a pole or zero at 0).

Matrix exponentials use expm::expm() (scaling and squaring with Pade approximation).

Examples

sys <- ctrl_ss(-1, 1, 1)
sysd <- ctrl_c2d(sys, 0.1)
sysd$A  # exp(-0.1)
#>           [,1]
#> [1,] 0.9048374
ctrl_c2d(ctrl_tf(1, c(1, 1, 0)), 0.5, method = "tustin")
#> Transfer function (discrete time, dt = 0.5)
#> 
#>    0.05 z^2 +   0.1 z +  0.05
#>   ---------------------------
#>      z^2 -   1.6 z +   0.6
